title: More of the photograph: Pritchett, Oscar Henry and others
summary: Francis names the trombonists, Old Man Delmore and others, and regrets giving away photographs.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: He works in that pressing shop on Rampart Street. He's wonderful too, yeah.
He's still up there then? He's still there, yeah.
I passed there and talked to him. Rampart about a block left off Canal Street on the Riverside. On the Riverside? A place named Grisby and Grisby, pressing shop.
Grisby, I'll have to...
Yeah. He's got some girls in there playing. He's wonderful, him.
Yeah, I see a couple girls on sax. Yeah. Oh, is that Old Man Barbaran? That's Old Man Barbaran, yeah. Old Man Barbaran.
Who's the other trombonist here?
Do you know? Yeah, that's Henry.
Sonny Henry?
No, not Sonny, that's Oscar Henry.
Sonny Henry's dead. I saw him this morning by the drip hook. I saw him this morning by the drip hook. I had a bunch of one on the convention.
That's Oscar Henry?
Oscar Henry, yeah.
He looks a little different than he does now.
He's small now.
The next one is a baritone horn, I guess. That trumpet looks familiar. I can't think who it would be though.
Where?
That's Pajot. No, in front there. I don't think anybody I know.
I can't make him up.
Red was playing trombone then.
That's Red Day. I brought this fellow one night from New Huygenson, he dropped there the next night.
Landry. Landry, yeah. I remember in 1949 he was playing at the Big Eye.
That's Old, I forgot this Old Man there.
Oh, down in front there.
Old Man Delmore, he used to be a professor too. On the tuba, is that it? No, on the bass, he was sitting down by the bass, he'd just direct the band, would preach it.
Oh yeah.
I had plenty of pictures of it bands, but I got rid of them, you know.
It's too bad you didn't save some of those old bands, they're hard to find now.
Old Man Bobberant died too.
Yeah, last summer, about a year ago.
